verifiedAgainstSpecText: Sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header are removed; GET and DELETE on the MCP endpoint answer 405 (streamable-http#earlier-streamable-http-revisions).

initialize/notifications/initialized are removed; every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion (required), io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (required) and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo (SHOULD) in _meta (basic/index#meta).

server/discover request shape (params._meta only) and DiscoverResult fields supportedVersions, capabilities, instructions, _meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo'], ttlMs, cacheScope (server/discover).

Mirrored headers MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name, their agreement with the body, the =?base64?...?= value encoding, Mcp-Param-{Name} from x-mcp-header, and the HeaderMismatch -32020 / MissingRequiredClientCapability -32021 / UnsupportedProtocolVersion -32022 codes (streamable-http#request-metadata, basic/index#error-codes).

x-mcp-header constraints: non-empty RFC 9110 token, case-insensitively unique, primitive types only (number excluded), statically reachable through properties chains only; a violating tool is excluded from tools/list (server/tools#x-mcp-header).
resultType discrimination: 'complete' and 'input_required'; an absent resultType from an earlier-revision server is treated as complete; an unrecognized value is invalid (basic/index#resulttype).

InputRequiredResult shape: inputRequests keyed by server-assigned ids with {method, params} limited to elicitation/create, sampling/createMessage and roots/list; opaque requestState echoed verbatim; at least one of the two present; the retry is the original request plus inputResponses under a new JSON-RPC id (basic/patterns/mrtr).
Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequest for a capability the client did not declare; clients MUST NOT inspect requestState (basic/patterns/mrtr#server-requirements-basic-workflow).

subscriptions/listen replaces the GET stream and resources/subscribe; notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged is first; every notification carries io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId equal to the listen request id (basic/patterns/subscriptions).
Streamable HTTP cancellation is closing the response stream; notifications/cancelled is stdio-only in this revision (basic/patterns/cancellation#transport-specific-cancellation).
No SSE resumability: Last-Event-ID and event ids are removed; a broken stream loses the in-flight request and it must be re-issued as a new request (changelog major change 9).

Cache hints ttlMs and cacheScope are required on complete results of server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list and resources/read; cacheScope 'private' must not be shared across authorization contexts; MRTR retries are not cacheable (server/utilities/caching).
Resource not found moved from -32002 to -32602, with -32002 still accepted from earlier revisions (server/resources#error-handling).

401 challenge with resource_metadata and scope; the well-known path-inserted and root fallbacks and their order; metadata resource must match; authorization_servers required (basic/authorization, .../authorization-server-discovery).

Client registration priority: pre-registered, then Client ID Metadata Documents when client_id_metadata_document_supported, then Dynamic Client Registration (deprecated in this revision), then prompting (basic/authorization/client-registration).
Tasks are an extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks) advertised under capabilities.extensions and negotiated, never assumed (basic/versioning#extension-negotiation).

Backward compatibility: a 400 whose body is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error identifies a legacy server; a recognized modern error means retry, not fall back (basic/versioning#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions, streamable-http#backward-compatibility).
inferredNotVerified: The unauthenticated probe used to read a challenge is a read-only tools/list; the specification does not prescribe which request a client should use to obtain a 401.
Treating an HTTP 202 in answer to a JSON-RPC request as 'no response will arrive' (the specification defines 202 only for notifications).
Clamping a server's ttlMs to a host maximum, and treating a negative or absent ttlMs as 0, follows the caching page's client guidance but the clamp itself is a host policy choice.
Bounding SSE streams by frame count and bytes, and bounding list pagination, are host policies; the specification sets no numeric limits.

verifiedAgainstSpecText: initialize carries protocolVersion, capabilities and clientInfo; the server answers with its own; notifications/initialized completes the handshake (basic/lifecycle).

MCP-Session-Id is assigned on the InitializeResult response, must be echoed on later requests, 400 when required and missing, 404 when expired (client must re-initialize), DELETE terminates, 405 when termination is not offered (basic/transports#session-management).
MCP-Protocol-Version on all requests after initialization; 400 on an unsupported value; absent means 2025-03-26 (basic/transports#protocol-version-header).

A POST response may be application/json or an SSE stream that carries server requests and notifications before the response; 202 acknowledges a notification or response; GET opens a standalone stream or answers 405 (basic/transports).

elicitation/create is a server-to-client request with form and url modes; the client answers action accept/decline/cancel; -32042 URLElicitationRequiredError and notifications/elicitation/complete exist in this revision only (client/elicitation).
Client ID Metadata Documents are SHOULD and Dynamic Client Registration is MAY, with the same four-step selection priority (basic/authorization).
inferredNotVerified: Reissuing a read-only request once after a 404 session expiry is a host policy; the specification only says the client must start a new session.

verifiedAgainstSpecText: Same handshake, session and protocol-version header rules as 2025-11-25, with capabilities limited to roots, sampling, elicitation and experimental on the client side.
Authorization in this revision documents pre-registration and Dynamic Client Registration; Client ID Metadata Documents are not part of it, which is what the capability rows report.
inferredNotVerified: Negotiating 2025-06-18 from a 2025-11-25 request (and the reverse) is treated as staying inside the legacy era; the specification describes version negotiation without naming eras.

limitations: The profile is selected by the binding's settings, never by the installed SDK version; the SDK is used only to build the legacy fixture server.
Auto-detection is off unless a binding sets compatibility to auto-detect; a pinned client refuses a server of the other era rather than accommodating it.
stdio transports are unsupported by design: a hosted connector launches no local process.
workItems.notes: Wire-log assertions in both fixture suites prove each profile's traffic contains only its own profile's messages, and that no single message carries both eras.

limitations: Completion (completion/complete) and logging are not implemented; they are not needed to bind an approved operation.
Resource subscriptions are read through a bounded listen stream; there is no durable event pipeline (that belongs to the events module).
workItems.notes: Cache keys are digests of tenant, owner, connection, generation, profile, era, negotiated version and credential reference, so a list a server labelled public is still never served to another principal.

limitations: Only form-mode elicitation is answered with values; URL mode produces a browser handoff for the initiating human and the client never fetches the URL.
A sampling request is refused rather than suspended, in either era.
Rounds are bounded (three by default); a server that keeps asking is failed, not looped.
workItems.notes: The pending request id, requested schema, opaque requestState, original arguments and round live in HandoffIssue.private; resumeInput re-checks binding revision, generation, destination, profile and handoff state, consumes the handoff one-use before calling, and returns no answer values.

limitations: Reconciliation of an indeterminate effect is the command layer's: this adapter records the uncertainty and refuses to repeat the call.
Retries exist only for reads and only for a request that was not delivered or whose response was lost; there is no retry budget for writes at all.
Protocol retries, HTTP retries and business reconciliation are separate: a repeated effect digest is answered from the journal without touching the network.
workItems.notes: sampling/createMessage is answered with a method-not-found error, roots/list with an empty list, unknown server requests with method-not-found; extensions are reported unsupported; header suggestions in _meta or annotations are ignored and flagged.

limitations: The four tools are a transport over a service the command swarm owns; they enforce projection and output policy, not authorization, which the service re-checks.
connector_invoke returns output only when the binding classified it public; personal and secret results are withheld from this transport and remain readable in the application.
workItems.notes: Registered only when createCeremonyMcpHandler is given the optional connectors option; the five existing tools and their tests are unchanged.

limitations: Live authorized evidence is blocked: no credentials for a deployed MCP server are available in this environment.
verify establishes that the credential was accepted by the origin and says explicitly that server identity is not attested beyond TLS.
authorize delegates to the OAuth swarm's beginOAuth hook; with a bearer already in custody it returns verify without contacting an authorization server.
disconnect is local only and revoke is unsupported: MCP defines no such operation.
workItems.notes: Capability rows report each revision's documented client-registration order, so a provider that requires legacy Dynamic Client Registration is served by the configured profile without claiming universal current behaviour.

integrationPatches.description: Applied additively in this branch: an optional `connectors?: ConnectorToolDependencies` option on CeremonyMcpOptions, and, inside build(), `if (options.connectors) registerConnectorServerTools(server, options.connectors, { actor: () => actor, ...(options.onerror ? { onerror: options.onerror } : {}) });`. Three insertions, no existing line changed; tests/mcp-server.test.ts passes unchanged (10/10).
Register createMcpRemoteAdapter({ beginOAuth, broker, cache }) from src/server/connectors/mcp/index.ts. Pass the shared McpResultCache so one cache serves every connection, keyed per principal.

Implement ConnectorToolDependencies (catalog(actor), status(actor, connectionRef), connect(actor, input), invoke(actor, input)) and pass it as the connectors option. Call the adapter's resumeInput(ctx, handoffRecord, values, action?) to continue a suspended MCP input; the handoff is consumed one-use inside it.

Provide BeginMcpOAuth: (ctx, { challenge, intent, resource, profile }) => Promise<AuthorizationStart>. The challenge carries the validated RFC 9728 metadata, the scopes the server named, the canonical resource identifier and the revision's client-registration order.
Optional: re-export src/server/connectors/mcp/index.ts from the server barrel. It is server-only (node:crypto, node:http-free but Buffer-using) and must not enter the browser bundle.

unmet.reason: Live-authorized evidence against a deployed MCP server is blocked: no authorized credentials exist in this environment. All rows are protocol-fixture.
AC-MCP-07 to AC-MCP-10 belong to the registry swarm; this ledger covers the runtime client, the adapter and the server tools only.
